A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AMORLIP work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and matchable, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original CC3M/CC12M pretraining experiments, downstream evaluation, efficiency measurements and ablations in Section 4, with additional task-level results in Figure 5.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and their results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–5, including the appendix breakdown.

M1.justification: The alternating amortization/encoder updates, lightweight MLPs, f-divergence and l2-log objectives, EMA targets and previous-epoch combination remain unchanged. Section 4.4 adds guidance for choosing existing components without changing the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions train on CC3M and CC12M and evaluate the same 38 DataComp tasks, including ImageNet shifts and image-text retrieval. V2 mentions fine-tuning only as a possible application of its guidance, not an evaluated task.

E2.justification: CLIP, SigLIP, SogCLR and FastCLIP remain the comparison methods in both scales of Table 1 and the convergence plots. No comparator is added, removed or substantively revised.

E3.justification: Both retain ResNet-50/CC3M training for 30 epochs with batch size 1024 and ViT-B/32/CC12M training for 33 epochs with batch size 2048. Sample counts, metrics and reported training settings are unchanged; Section 4.4's recommendations do not revise the existing experimental protocols.

E4.justification: The update-frequency, network-capacity, EMA, combination-weight, objective and amortization-target analyses are retained with identical evidence. Section 4.4 interprets existing ablations rather than adding new sensitivity or robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2's checklist item 7 explicitly acknowledges the absence of error bars but introduces no statistical estimates or changes in reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the plotted results in Figures 1–5 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains AMORLIP(l2-log)'s 38-task averages of 24.11% and 30.66%, versus CLIP's 21.48% and 27.65%, respectively. No experimental result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Proposition 1, objectives and Appendix B derivations remain unchanged, including the second-order relationship between the divergence objectives. Moving the EBM background equation into Section 5 does not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: lightweight partition-function amortization, reduced large-batch dependence, improved efficiency and performance across 38 tasks with relative improvements up to 12.24%.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 adds conditional advice favoring l2-log when temperature varies and suggesting f-divergence may work better with stable temperature, such as fine-tuning. It also interprets the ablations as reducing tuning needs. The checklist newly acknowledges missing error bars; Appendix A's existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 adds explicit setup recommendations, including infrequent amortization updates and smaller network widths, with guidance on objective selection. These supplement existing settings rather than document changed runs. Optimizer details, hardware and the code link are retained, with v1 Appendix D becoming v2 Appendix C.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Vision Transformer reference, An Image Is Worth 16x16 Words, cited in the assets checklist. The EBM discussion moves unchanged from v1 Appendix C into Section 5, so it is not a new expansion of research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 largely preserves the existing prose while adding Section 4.4, acknowledgments, author contact information and the NeurIPS checklist. It moves EBM related work into the main text and renumbers the remaining appendices, constituting limited narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: The same five figures and three tables retain their artwork, axes, legends and structures. Spacing and placement change locally; Figure 5 and its explanatory appendix text now share a page instead of leaving the explanation on a nearly empty separate page.

improvement.justification: Section 4.4 makes existing ablations more actionable through explicit setup recommendations, while the relocated EBM discussion and improved appendix layout aid navigation. These are modest usability gains. The scientific evidence is unchanged, the fine-tuning recommendation remains untested, and the new acknowledgment of missing error bars does not resolve that limitation.
